brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.evidence: 3-cell cluster (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full) with 3 bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments for small notions like buttons/beads), bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments for thread/bobbins), bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full (large compartment for fabric/large spools), plus accessory:0#0,0#1 rod for spool handling and two hooks accessory:0#1,0#0 and accessory:0#0,1#0 for scissors/tape. Joints locked and faces capped.

Configurator repeatedly returned BUSY/TIMED_OUT when settling props in bins (e.g., ruler, tape-gaffer, tweezers) so visual props could not be placed, despite mesh-clear hardware. Build shape supports staging but props not shown.

finish.summary: Compact 3-cell sewing caddy: three bins giving 6 compartments total (3+2+1) for sorting small notions, thread and fabric, with side hooks and rod for hanging tools. Hardware verified mesh-clear; prop placement was blocked by configurator BUSY timeouts.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
